title: Damp room, dry room
hook: Same temperature, 40% or 80% humidity: how much weaker is the drying push?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that at the same temperature, the more water vapour already in the air, the weaker the push for water to leave the cloth, so drying slows in humid air

misconception: Humid air hardly slows drying; warmth is what matters.
objective: At equal temperature, higher relative humidity means a smaller difference between a wet surface’s saturation vapour pressure and surrounding water vapour. This model shows the gap, not a drying clock.

claims.text: At the same temperature, humid air already holds close to all the water vapour it can, so it takes water from a wet surface more slowly. The push is how far the air is from full.
claims.source: OpenStax College Physics 2e §13.6, https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/13-6-humidity-evaporation-and-boiling (opened 2026-10-14). Evaporation is inhibited by humidity. The card's constant flux is an explicitly illustrative assumption, not a measured household drying rate. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Opened OpenStax §13.6 (m42219): 'Relative humidity is related to the partial pressure of water vapor in the air. At 100% humidity, the partial pressure is equal to the vapor pressure ... If the partial pressure is less than the vapor pressure, then evaporation will take place'; 'evaporation is inhibited by high humidity'. At fixed temperature the saturation vapour pressure is fixed and partial pressure = RH x saturation pressure, so the gap is p_sat(1 - RH) and shrinks as RH rises. 'Shows the gap, not a drying clock': engine case 'humidity' computes only value = 1 - RH/100, labelled 'Normalised gap', with no time output. Reset to unverified 2026-10-15 by demo-builder (r11 fix plan wave W2: new prediction line, stage and reveal; engine 2). Re-verify against the rebuilt stage. | FC pass 52 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, W-1144/W2): VERIFIED. OpenStax College Physics 2e §13.6, opened 2026-10-16 as the book's CNXML source (github.com/openstax/osbooks-college-physics-bundle, modules/m42219/index.cnxml via raw.githubusercontent.com, sha256 4d622c5f94e2…; openstax.org itself is blocked here): 'Relative humidity is related to the partial pressure of water vapor in the air. At 100% humidity, the partial pressure is equal to the vapor pressure, and no more water can enter the vapor phase. If the partial pressure is less than the vapor pressure, then evaporation will take place'; 'At its maximum, denoted as saturation, the relative humidity is 100%, and evaporation is inhibited.' At one temperature, RH is the share of the saturation amount, so 80% air is close to full and the gap to full (the card's 'push') is smaller. Matches the claim.

claims.text: Surface temperature, airflow and fabric also matter; no room-control advice is implied.

recall.question: Two rooms are at the same temperature: one at 40% humidity, one at 80%. In the lesson's model, how does the drying push compare?
options: Equal, since both rooms are at the same temperature
Twice as strong in the 40% room
Three times as strong in the 40% room
recall.why: In this model the push is how far the air is from full: 100 − 40 = 60 points in the drier room and 100 − 80 = 20 in the humid one, three times as strong. A weaker push means slower evaporation. This is not a drying clock.
